piece: VOP3 output and source modifiers in the game's forms, on RDNA2
sentences: Every distinct float VALU form in the 26,503 listings that carries `clamp`, an omod (`mul:2`/`mul:4`/`div:2`), `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi` or neg/abs: 572 forms, 1,270,932 instructions (`v_mul_legacy_f32 … clamp` alone is 147,499; `v_fma_mix_f32` has 222 forms), up to 120 random operand triples each, run natively on gfx1036 (`tools/hw_oracle`, the game's MODE) and through the translator: 542 forms, 64,802 cases (the GFX10.1-only `v_mad_f32`/`v_mad_legacy_f32`/`v_mac_f32` and `v_permlanex16` are left out). 51,761 give the translator's word.

The rest are differences already on record: NaN sign and payload (5,074); f32 denormal operands or results, and a denormal intermediate that the hardware flushes before the omod or clamp (1,178; SHADER-377); an omod turning a -0 result into +0 (121; the Output modifiers rows, #1281); 1 ulp or the known sin/cos precision in `v_rcp/v_rcp_iflag/v_log/v_sin/v_cos` with an omod (56); and 6,430 whose translation is undefined in SPIR-V, mostly `FClamp` of a NaN, where the hardware gives +0 under DX10_CLAMP (#2437). 182 cases were my harness's (three distinct SGPRs, over GFX10's two-read limit).
`tests/semantic/test_alu_vop3_mods_hw.py` replays 1,616 matching words, up to three per form; it fails without `clamp` (326 rows) or without the omod (237).
